transcript.text: Wanted to put this in front of you first: over the trailing 30-day window this wallet has closed 4007 trades at a 53.88% win rate, and it's done that while paying 8053 in fees — that's 2.01 a trade, so the turnover is real, not a couple of lucky prints. Same wallet, last 7 days: 424 closed trades at a 100% win rate for 35723 realized. That's the screen you run, and it clears it.

High turnover with plausible win rate over 30 days is decent evidence of a real, active strategy. But 100% win rate over 424 trades in 7 days is a major red flag — that's statistically implausible for any genuine trading strategy and suggests either cherry-picked data, wash trading, or an unsustainable/manipulated pattern (or misreporting). I'll size a moderate position based on the credible 30-day track record, but withhold larger allocation until the anomalous 7-day claim is explained or reconciled.

ALLOCATION: 25

The thing that should matter more to you is breadth. Breadth across uncorrelated instruments does strengthen the case that this is a systematic process rather than a single lucky bet — that's meaningful evidence. But it doesn't resolve my core concern: a 100% win rate over 424 trades in 7 days remains statistically anomalous regardless of how diversified the book is. That kind of perfection, even spread across instruments, is more consistent with wash trading, cherry-picked reporting, or a data/methodology issue than genuine edge. Breadth mitigates concentration risk but doesn't validate accuracy of the reported numbers.

I'll increase sizing modestly given the multi-instrument consistency in the 30-day data, but I'm still capping well below full commitment until the 7-day anomaly is explained.

ALLOCATION: 35

That's a reasonable structure — a starting position sized well below conviction level, with scale-up contingent on the anomaly resolving or repeating cleanly next cycle. It respects the unresolved 100% win-rate flag while not ignoring genuinely decent breadth and turnover evidence.
